headline: Mantas after dark, dinner at *9,000 ft*.
footer: {nights} nights on the dry side of the Big Island, then Miami.

paragraphs: The Big Island rather than Oahu, because the manta night dive is off Kona and nowhere near Honolulu. About 200,000 people on an island bigger than all the others put together, and an open-air airport where everyone walks down the stairs into the sun.
Three days have something in them. The others are free, and the cards further down are for those, or for nothing.

notes.lead: Diving and altitude do not mix.
notes.rest: Both Mauna Kea operators refuse anyone who has been on scuba in the previous 24 hours, and the flight home wants a clear day too. That is what sets the order: underwater Tuesday and Wednesday, the mountain on Thursday, dry land after.
Kailua-Kona, up the hill from the bay, from 15:00 on Sunday the 6th to 10:00 on Sunday the 13th. The dive shops and the town car rental are a short walk away.

notes.lead: A car for one day, not seven.
notes.rest: Everything in town is on foot or on the Kona Trolley, the boats and the mountain are rides, and Saturday is the one day that needs wheels.

notes.lead: Mornings are for work, for whoever is working.
notes.rest: Kona is 5 hours behind Miami, so a 9:00 Miami start is 4:00 here and the workday is over by lunch.

sections.title: The shape of the week
sections.note: Three days with something in them.

items.detail: A ride from KOA, about 20 minutes, and the house from 15:00. Sunset on the seawall if the flight allows.
Down the hill to Aliʻi Drive, the trolley to Kahalu‘u to snorkel with the turtles, and getting over the Pacific.

One boat for both of us from Honokōhau. Two tanks for Os, a day dive then the mantas after dark, and Jabari snorkels them from the surface under the same lights. Kaloko-Honokōhau is next to the harbour for before.
Discover Scuba, boat out around 8:30 and back by 13:00. Os dives the same boat or takes the morning off. Huliheʻe Palace reopens on Wednesdays, for the afternoon.
Picked up in town early afternoon, back around 22:00. More than 24 hours after the dive, which is the rule. The whole evening is below.
Town, the palace, the market, Magic Sands if the sand is in, or nothing.
Picked up in town between 9:00 and 12:00. South to the coffee farms, the place of refuge and Two Step, or the long drive to Volcanoes. Not both.
Car back at KOA on the way to the flight, and on to Miami. Sunday is the likely day; the tickets are not bought yet.

sections.headline: Dinner at 9,000 ft, then *the sky*.

steps.detail: Pickup in town, then a 4WD van up the mountain, which rental cars are not allowed to drive.
Dinner at the mid-level station, partly for the food and partly to adjust to the height.
Sunset from the summit, around 17:45, above the clouds and among the big research observatories. Parkas and gloves are provided, because it is close to freezing up there.
A telescope session with hot drinks, on 11-inch scopes.

compare.name: Hawaiʻi Forest & Trail
rows: King Kamehameha, walkable from town, early afternoon
Warm picnic dinner at about 9,200 ft

compare.name: Mauna Kea Summit Adventures
rows: Kona Crossroads at 13:55, a short ride up the hill
Hot lasagna and a brownie at the visitor station
24 hours’ notice, no refund inside that

compare.name: Taikobo Signature Tour
rows: Their office up the hill, early afternoon
None, snacks only, so eat first
$50 each back if cloud spoils the stars

sections.note: All four include summit sunset, parkas, transport and a telescope session, and all refuse anyone who has been on scuba in the previous 24 hours. Hawaiʻi Forest & Trail is the pick: the only pickup we can walk to, the smallest group, and the photos to keep. For two people it comes to roughly $720 to $760 with tax and a tip. Nobody near Kona runs a telescope-only night without the summit that works without a car. The new moon is on the 8th, so Thursday is about as dark as the mountain gets.

sections.title: Getting around
sections.note: No car for six of the seven days.

items.name: The house
items.where: Up the hill from the bay
items.detail: About 20 minutes on foot down to Aliʻi Drive, and the same back up, slower. Kona Brewing, the dive shops and the Enterprise office are all close.

items.name: From the airport
items.detail: Uber or Lyft, reportedly $25 to $45. There is no car to collect, which is the point.

items.name: The Kona Trolley
items.detail: Along Aliʻi Drive between the Target park and ride and Keauhou, hourly from 6:00 to 21:00, every day. Magic Sands and Kahalu‘u are both on it. It was free until the end of 2025, and whether it still is in 2026 was not clear.

items.name: The dive boats
items.detail: No shop picks up. A ride is roughly $15 to $22, and the manta boat is back around 21:00, when drivers are scarce, so the ride home is worth booking ahead. Kona Taxicab is 808-324-4444.

items.name: The car
items.detail: Saturday hours are only 9:00 to 12:00, it is closed on Sunday, and there are no after-hours returns. Returning it at KOA on the way to the flight fits, if a one-way return is allowed. Economy is roughly $60 to $90 a day.

sections.intro: The house is done. Five things left, roughly in the order they stop being easy.

items.label: The flights
items.detail: Out on Sunday the 13th, most likely, landing in Miami on Monday. Not bought yet, and an overnight connection that lands at 5:00 is worth avoiding.

items.label: The Mauna Kea tour
items.detail: Hawaiʻi Forest & Trail for Thursday the 10th, about $720 to $760 for two with tax and a tip. Twelve seats, and the new moon is on the 8th, so the week is in demand. Worth checking the pickup time at checkout.

items.label: The manta boat
items.detail: Tuesday afternoon, one diver and one snorkeller in a single booking, so both land on the same boat.

items.label: Discover Scuba
items.detail: Wednesday morning. The PADI medical form comes first, and any yes on it needs a doctor’s sign-off, so it is worth reading well before December.

items.label: The Saturday car
items.detail: The town office has three hours on a Saturday, so it goes early.

sections.caveat: Operator prices were checked on their own sites in September 2026 and are before tax. Ride fares, the car rate, the trolley fare and food prices are estimates. Hurricane Nolo closed the park and the Mauna Kea visitor station for a few days in late September; both are worth checking again in November.
